solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Robust compilers are going to do our job (4-3)

blocks.note: a crossword compiler's job is to set puzzles

annotation.surface: The setters boast that they are about to get down to work.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a sentence the setters say about themselves: we'll set.
annotation.definitionFit: A well-set person has a solid, sturdy build, which is what robust describes.

entries.clue: 1980s band welcoming a day in Oxford college (6)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the band takes the letters in, as a host welcomes guests through the door

annotation.surface: A pop group from the eighties spends a day playing at an Oxford college.
annotation.walkthrough: The inserted pair lands right after the band's first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Wadham, founded in 1610, is one of the constituent colleges of Oxford University.

entries.clue: Small, fast runner always obstructed by obstacle (7)

indicatorNotes.obstructed by: the obstacle blocks the word in on both sides, hemming it in

blocks.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

annotation.surface: A quick little runner keeps being tripped up by a hurdle.
annotation.walkthrough: The old sense of let as an obstruction survives in tennis and in legal phrases.
annotation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare: small because it is a baby, fast because hares are.

entries.clue: Location of websites grasped by visionary poet (9)

indicatorNotes.grasped by: the seer holds the phrase inside his grip, so it goes within him

annotation.surface: A prophetic poet has a firm grip on where websites live.

annotation.definitionFit: A sonneteer writes sonnets, fourteen-line poems, so is a kind of poet.

entries.clue: Doctrine unaffected by revolution? (5)

indicatorNotes.unaffected by revolution: turned end to end, the word comes out exactly the same

annotation.surface: A belief so firm that no uprising could shake it.
annotation.walkthrough: Revolution suggests politics; here it means turning the word round.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle held as true by a church or school of thought.

entries.clue: Mixed drink prior to winning fight (5-2)

blocks.note: up = ahead, as in two goals up

annotation.surface: A bowl of punch gets drunk just before a brawl breaks out.
annotation.walkthrough: Mixed looks like an anagram signal, but it only describes the drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A punch-up is British slang for a brawl with fists.

entries.clue: Coax salesman over petition to limit publicity (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, turned over means the word is read upwards
indicatorNotes.to limit: the petition hems the publicity in, keeping it within bounds

blocks.note: to sue is to petition a court

annotation.surface: A salesman gets round a petition that would restrict advertising.
annotation.walkthrough: Over reads as 'about' in the surface; in a down clue it flips the salesman.
annotation.definitionFit: To coax is to win someone round gently, by talk rather than force.

entries.clue: Jog, say, with horse heading north (5)

indicatorNotes.heading north: in a down clue, travelling north means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse

annotation.surface: A rider jogs along on a horse pointing north.
annotation.walkthrough: Jog looks like running, but here it is the verb for a little push.
annotation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to give it a light push, as a reminder.

entries.clue: Colour lines somewhat regular (7)

indicatorNotes.lines: the colour lines the phrase, as fabric lines a coat, so it wraps round it

annotation.surface: Coloured lines on a page look fairly regular.
annotation.walkthrough: Lines looks like a noun; it is the verb, and regular is a noun too.
annotation.definitionFit: A habitué is someone who frequents a place, like a regular at a pub.

entries.clue: Point legal duty out — one may do so in court (5,3,6)

annotation.definition: one may do so in court

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are put out of their order, as a bone is put out of joint

annotation.surface: A defendant points out that he had no legal duty, as one might in court.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom surface makes the whole clue read as legal argument, so the answer sits naturally in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A defendant answering a charge at trial enters a plea, and denying it is one plea open to them.

entries.clue: Kelly, in films, gets a lot of credit dealing with make-up (7)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of the word but not all of it, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Gene Kelly, star of Singin' in the Rain
TICK = credit, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A film star earns plenty on account from his work in the make-up department.
annotation.walkthrough: Buying on tick is old British slang for buying on credit. Make-up here is genetic make-up, not cosmetics.
annotation.definitionFit: Genetic concerns genes, the inherited code that sets a creature's biological constitution.

entries.clue: Rising mist round delta area by the River Don (9)

indicatorNotes.Rising: in a down clue, a rising word is read upwards
indicatorNotes.round: the upturned mist goes round the delta letter
indicatorNotes.by: the rest is set beside it, following on

blocks.note: D is delta in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Fog lifts from a delta near a river called the Don.
annotation.walkthrough: The River Don is a real river in Yorkshire, which disguises Don as a Mafia boss.
annotation.definitionFit: In Mafia usage a don is a boss, and The Godfather made that title famous.

entries.clue: Nearly ignoring nobleman recalling sight seen on safari? (5)

blocks.note: à la = in the style of, so recalling

annotation.walkthrough: Nearly looks like 'almost'; it is the word to be emptied of the nobleman.
annotation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope, one of the animals tourists hope to spot.

entries.clue: Swallow vermouth, dishonest over drink? Don’t object (4,2,5,4)

blocks.note: It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

annotation.surface: Someone knocks back vermouth and lies about their drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just stacks one piece above the next. The definition is an imperative.
annotation.definitionFit: To take something lying down is to accept an insult meekly, without protest.

entries.clue: Caught heron hiding head in wooden box with strings (7)

blocks.note: BITTERN, a heron, without its B

annotation.walkthrough: The bittern is a kind of heron. The box with strings is a musical instrument, not a cage.
annotation.definitionFit: The cittern is a Renaissance plucked instrument: a wooden body strung with wire.

entries.clue: Eating around 6, party first in restaurant sent back staff to find water (8,3)

indicatorNotes.around: the eating word goes around the number, enclosing it
indicatorNotes.first in: take the opening letter of restaurant only
indicatorNotes.sent back: the party and letter return, so read them backwards

annotation.surface: A restaurant party sends its food back to the staff and asks for water.
annotation.walkthrough: Staff means a stick, not waiters, and the 6 refers to nothing in the grid: it is a Roman numeral.
annotation.definitionFit: Dowsers walk with a forked stick that is said to dip over underground water.

entries.clue: Place for rolls of cash head of bank takes out (11)

indicatorNotes.head of: the head is the front, so take the first letter of bank
indicatorNotes.out: the letters of takes are put out of their order

annotation.surface: A bank manager withdraws rolls of banknotes.
annotation.walkthrough: Rolls of cash suggests banknotes; the rolls are bread rolls.
annotation.definitionFit: Bread rolls are served at the table in a small basket.

entries.clue: Match about to occupy a long time (5)

indicatorNotes.to occupy: the word moves into the long time and fills its middle, as troops occupy a town

annotation.surface: A sports fixture looks set to drag on for ages.
annotation.walkthrough: Match is the verb, as two witness accounts match, not a sporting fixture.
annotation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match correspond with each other in every detail.

entries.clue: Under most stress, and kind of cross before ordeal (7)

annotation.surface: Someone at breaking point and angry ahead of a trial.
annotation.walkthrough: Cross looks like an adjective for angry; it is the noun, a T-shaped cross.

entries.clue: Embroider an accessory worn by son after little drink (9)

indicatorNotes.worn by: the son wears the tie, so the tie goes round his letter
indicatorNotes.after: the accessory and son come after the drink

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
a tie is a neck accessory

annotation.walkthrough: Embroider means to exaggerate a story here, not needlework.

entries.clue: Player who, to resolve a pay dispute, made the issue vanish? (3,4,5,2,7)

annotation.definition: Player who, to resolve a pay dispute, made the issue vanish?

blocks.clueFragment: Player who, to resolve a pay dispute,
blocks.note: the player is a musician, cheated of his fee by a town
issue = offspring; the town's children disappear

annotation.surface: A negotiator settles a wage row by making the problem disappear.
annotation.walkthrough: Player means a musician; issue means children. Unpaid for ridding the town of rats, the piper led its children away.
annotation.definitionFit: In the legend the piper, refused his fee after luring away the rats, piped the town's children into a mountain.

entries.clue: One books trio playing religious music (7)

indicatorNotes.after: this piece is placed after the others in the answer

entries.clue: Like some lodges with family members in charge (7)

blocks.note: a mother and a son, two members of a family

annotation.surface: Holiday lodges run by a family.
annotation.walkthrough: Lodges suggests holiday cabins; here it means a branch of a society.

entries.clue: Return strange material for jewellery (8)
